comments.note: The WP spec referenced 'composer test-suite -- api-cache', but phpunit.xml defines only a single suite ('Framework Tests'). The correct command for targeting cache tests is 'composer test-file -- tests/AppFrameworkTests/API/Cache/'. The test-suite script passes --testsuite to PHPUnit, so an unrecognised suite name silently produces 'No tests executed' instead of an error — this could be misleading. Consider either adding named suites to phpunit.xml or updating the WP template to use test-file/test-filter for path-based test targeting.

19+ test class files emit 'Class X cannot be found' warnings when running test-filter with any pattern. These are pre-existing autoload/classmap issues in the test directory (e.g. tests/AppFrameworkTests/Application/Messagelogs.php, tests/AppFrameworkTests/Collection/IntegerRecord.php). The PHPUnit exit code becomes 1 even when no actual test failures occur, making CI harder to interpret. Root cause: test classes use short, non-namespaced names that clash with PHPUnit's class-finder heuristics.

comments.note: CacheableAPIMethodTrait::readFromCache() — If AppFactory::createLogger()->logError() itself throws (e.g. logger initialisation failure), the exception would escape readFromCache() rather than falling through to 'return null'. The logError() call is not wrapped in the inner defensive try/catch that guards the delete. In practice the framework logger is stable, so this is an unlikely path, but for maximum resilience the log call could be moved inside the inner try/catch or wrapped in its own. Non-blocking.

summary: All six implementation changes reviewed against all four Review Dimensions. No blocking issues found.

WP-001 (CacheableAPIMethodTrait): logError() placed correctly before delete-retry. sprintf with %d for error code is type-safe. ERROR_CACHE_FILE_CORRUPT constant is now live (no longer dead code). AppFactory import was already present. Recovery behaviour unchanged.

WP-002 (AI FixedDurationStrategy): isCacheFileValid() exactly mirrors the API counterpart pattern. Protected visibility is intentional and correct (strategy inheritance hierarchy vs. interface). PHPDoc matches API counterpart. strict === false guard is sound.
WP-003 (APICacheManager::invalidateMethod): @throws APICacheException annotation present and correctly documents the propagated exception from the delegated getMethodCacheFolder() call.

WP-004 (module-context-reference.md): Keyword Syntax Constraints section is placed immediately after the keywords subsection for maximum discoverability. Warning callout, correct/incorrect examples, and consequence all present.

WP-005 (CountryRequestScreen): Placed at TestDriver\\Area\\TestingScreen\\ — correctly following actual test-app conventions rather than the WP's preliminary path suggestion. Registered in sitemap. PHPDoc clearly states the class exists as a PHPStan consumer. _renderContent() calls getCountryRequest() so PHPStan analyses the method body too, not just the interface signature.

WP-006 (constraints.md Trait Consumer Policy): Section present with clear rule, rationale (PHPStan blind spot), procedure, and a concrete reference example (CountryRequestScreen). Well aligned with the project's shift away from suppression-based workarounds.

comments.note: CacheableAPIMethodTrait::readFromCache() — The logError() call is not itself wrapped in a defensive try/catch. If AppFactory::createLogger() were to throw (e.g. during framework bootstrap failure), the exception would escape the outer catch block rather than falling through to `return null`. In practice the framework logger is a stable singleton and this path is unreachable in production, but for maximum resilience the log call could be enclosed in its own try/catch. Carry-forward from QA pipeline. Non-blocking.

AI FixedDurationStrategy::isCacheFileValid() — No dedicated unit test exercises the filemtime()===false edge path added in WP-002. The broader 44-test 'Cache' filter confirms no regressions, and PHPStan validates the guard's type correctness. A dedicated test that stubs a JSONFile whose path does not exist would formalise the regression spec. Non-blocking.

CountryRequestTrait uses if(!isset($this->countryRequest)) as its lazy-init guard. For a nullable typed property, isset() returns false both when null and when uninitialised, so the guard is correct. An explicit === null check would be more expressive, but this is stylistic and fully consistent with existing project patterns. Non-blocking.

Pre-existing: 19 test class files emit PHPUnit class-discovery warnings (non-namespaced short names clashing with PHPUnit classloader heuristics), causing test-filter to return exit code 1 even when all tests pass.
